originality.rationale: Direct comparison with the accessible primary incidence-rarefaction framework distinguishes full sampling-law equivalence from the known weaker identity of mean accumulation curves. Searches of published-finding corpus and literature did not find a matching four-by-four first collision under connected twin-free assumptions. Structural neighborhood-hypergraph literature not fully accessed remains a risk, and absence from searches is not a novelty proof.

value.rationale: Sample-based richness distributions are standard ecological summaries. Demonstrating the sharp smallest connected, twin-free incidence networks where even the entire distribution at every effort level cannot determine network organization gives a motivated structural identifiability boundary, stronger than known mean-curve ambiguity. Matching both degree distributions rules out a cheap explanation. Relevance is to finite information loss, not necessarily empirical detectability.
